definition: The point through which all the weight of an object can be taken to act; for a uniform object it lies on every line of symmetry (at the centre of a uniform ruler, rectangular sheet or ring), and it can lie outside the material, as for a ring.

How hard it is to tip an object over; an object is more stable when its centre of gravity is lower or its base is wider, and it topples once the vertical line through its centre of gravity passes outside its base.
